subject: sex-specific models: sessions with only one sex

messages.author: c9959328f1f36ff7
messages.subject: sex-specific models: sessions with only one sex
parts:
Dear SECR Users,

I am looking at the effects of density on mice spacing behavior using SECR models (as nicely introducded by Effrod et al. 2015). I
So far, I worked on females-only data and got quite interesting results. 
However, I would like to fit the models to whole data set (females and males) since I am worried about potential bias of not including all trapped individuals (males still occupy live-traps, which could bias estimates, right?). 
On the other hand, there are other rodent species on grids so it would not resolve the problem anyway... Still, I would like to see the results for males as well. And see how/if inclusion of males changes the results. 
The problem is that I am working with strongly fluctuating rodent populations so there are sessions in which only one sex was captured. 

This is producing the warning message:
1: In verify.capthist(capthist, report = 1) :
  Levels of factor covariate(s) differ between session

Is there a way to overcome this? Or I should just run separete models for each sex?

Thanks for your help!

very best,
Michał
